Not as an adult, but as a teen I did jury duty as a volunteer.

It was called Teen Court, and the idea was that juveniles who committed minor crimes could get their offense taken off their record if they opted to face a jury of their peers in court. Teens acted as lawyers, the bailiff, the clerk and the jury, with a real, adult judge. Teen volunteers got to see how a courtroom operates and they learned about the law, while the convicted got to clean their record if they completed whatever rehabilitative assignments the jury assigned them.

I sat on a jury once for a domestic violence case. It is terrifying that my fate may one day be decided by a group of people this stupid.

Another guy (an ex heroin addict) claimed that in his experience, when people have guns put in their mouthes, they end up with broken teeth, and the victim didn't, so he didn't think it happened. This is despite the fact that the defendant was attempting to claim that she put the gun in her own mouth that night. So both parties say the gun was in her mouth, this guy still didn't believe it.

We ended up with a hung jury because one guy, from the get-go, was convinced that the victim was lying because "women lie all the time." He managed to get the ex-junkie and idiot woman to vote not guilty.

Juries are scary. It felt like a roll of the dice rather than a controlled process.
